question: A startup's Next.js app needs five endpoints to read and write the app's own data, used only by that frontend. What is the most pragmatic choice?
options: A separate NestJS service with its own deployment
Next.js route handlers (or server actions) in the same project, extracted later if other clients appear
An Express server inside a Next.js API route
explanation: When one frontend is the only client, co-located handlers avoid a second deployment and share types. A separate service pays off when other clients, teams or long-running work appear.

question: A new API must run on Cloudflare Workers today and maybe in a Node container later. Which framework fits best?
explanation: Hono is built on Web Standards `Request`/`Response`, so the same app runs on Workers, Node (through an adapter), Bun, Deno and serverless. Express, Koa and Fastify are bound to `node:http`.

question: An engineering organization of 40 developers wants every service to look the same, with dependency injection and generated OpenAPI docs. Which option matches that goal?
explanation: NestJS trades flexibility for enforced structure (modules, controllers, providers, DI) and ships OpenAPI integration, which suits large teams that value consistency.

question: A teammate wants to migrate a stable Express API to Fastify "because benchmarks show it is 3× faster". The API spends 90% of each request waiting for PostgreSQL. What is the best response?
options: The framework overhead is a small part of the latency; measure first and optimize queries, indexes or caching before a costly migration
explanation: Framework benchmarks measure trivial requests. When the database dominates, a migration buys little; profiling and query work pay off more.

question: An AI assistant generates `app.use(bodyParser.json())` and wraps every async route in `try { ... } catch (err) { next(err) }` for a project on Express 5. What does this tell you?
options: The code is the recommended Express 5 style
It is Express 4-era code: Express 5 has `express.json()` built in and forwards rejected promises to the error handler; tell the assistant the version
Express 5 does not support JSON bodies
It means the project should switch to Fastify
explanation: Assistants are trained on years of older code. Stating the framework version and pasting an existing route keeps generated code idiomatic.
